$comment: Shared parity fixture for the early-access resolver.
Read by BOTH implementations' test suites:
The API enforces this server-side and the clients gate UI with it. If the
two implementations disagree, a user sees a feature the server then refuses
to serve, or vice versa. Add cases here rather than to one suite alone.
`now` and `earlyAccessUntil` are ISO-8601. `earlyAccessUntil: null` means the
feature has no config row, or a row that never placed it under early access.
Note what is NOT modelled here: 'we could not resolve the signals'. This
resolver is a pure decision over inputs it trusts to be resolved already.
Callers own the unresolved case and must deny - see the fail-closed guard in

cases.name: no config row — generally available, free for everyone
no config row — Pro member also allowed
window passed — graduated to free for all
inside the window — non-Pro is gated
inside the window — Pro member is allowed
expiry exactly equals now — boundary counts as graduated
one millisecond before expiry — still gated
unparseable timestamp — treated as no window, not as gated
